headline: Democrats' gains, a Brampton plant fight and Nvidia's CEO exit mark the week
summary: Democrats added a Mississippi Senate seat and the Kansas governorship to their midterm sweep, then opened a leadership contest of their own. Hopes for an Iran deal rose and faded, sending oil back toward US$96, and U.S. wholesale inflation hit 6.5%. In Ontario, Stellantis's sale of the Brampton plant set off a confrontation with Ottawa that may end in court, the province named powerful new regional chairs, and a Microsoft email outage disrupted Toronto hospitals and schools.

top.headline: Democrats' sweep grows; Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate leader
top.what: Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's Senate seat on Wednesday and the Associated Press called the Kansas governor's race for Democrat Cindy Holscher on Thursday, with Alaska's Senate race still uncalled. On Thursday night Sen. Chris Van Hollen said he will run against Chuck Schumer for majority leader in a Dec. 1 vote.
top.why: Control of Congress changes in January, which affects tariffs, oversight of the White House and U.S. policy toward Canada.

top.headline: Iran deal hopes fade as Trump says none is needed; oil rebounds
top.what: Brent dipped below US$90 on Tuesday on hopes for a deal, then settled at US$95.82 on Thursday after Trump said the U.S. needs no agreement and pulled Vance off the talks. Iran reported tankers hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz, and Israel's cabinet reportedly ordered readiness for a strike; oil is still down for the week.
top.why: Oil prices drive gas costs and inflation in Canada, and with them the Bank of Canada's next rate move.

top.headline: Ottawa and Stellantis head toward court over Brampton plant sale
top.what: Stellantis announced the sale of its idled Brampton plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel on Monday. By Thursday Ottawa had started a 30-day default clock, rejected a $24-million repayment offer and threatened to sue; talks now move to the company's global chief executive.
top.why: Laid-off GTA auto workers and hundreds of millions in public subsidies are at stake.

top.headline: U.S. wholesale inflation reaches 6.5%, highest since 2022
top.what: U.S. producer prices rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% over the year, and stocks fell Friday morning as investors weighed the chance of a Federal Reserve rate increase in December.
top.why: Higher U.S. rates tend to pull Canadian mortgage and bond rates up with them.

top.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns amid reports of a Chinese intelligence link
top.what: Huang quit as chief executive on Thursday after reports about a relationship with a woman U.S. officials reportedly believe worked for Chinese intelligence; finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO and he has agreed to testify to a House committee.
top.why: Nvidia is among the most widely held stocks in Canadian pension and index funds, and the case may tighten U.S. chip export rules.

top.headline: Ontario names 'strong chairs' for eight regions, including York and Peel
top.what: The province appointed regional heads with powers to veto some bylaws, propose budgets and hire or fire senior staff, among them Vaughan Mayor Steven Del Duca in York; several mayors and a replaced chair objected.
top.why: The appointees, not voters, now steer budgets and property-tax decisions across most of the GTA from Nov. 15.

top.headline: Microsoft email outage hits Toronto hospitals, schools and City Hall
top.what: An Outlook failure on Thursday led Unity Health Toronto to declare a Code Grey and disrupted universities, City Hall and VIA Rail; service was gradually returning Friday with no confirmed root cause.
top.why: It showed how many essential services depend on a single company's online email.

top.headline: U.S. envoys meet Putin and Zelenskyy; Europe promised a seat but has no negotiator
top.what: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Putin in Moscow and briefed Zelenskyy near Dublin on Thursday without a breakthrough, agreeing Europe will join the next round. EU leaders meeting Friday had not agreed on who would represent them.
top.why: A settlement, or its failure, shapes European security, defence spending and Canada's commitments to Ukraine.
